name: @oyah/mcp

tools.name: read_board
tools.description: Read the live Oyah board as JSON. With no narrowing it returns an INDEX: every outcome (ref, title, status, measure) and its Steps as ref, title, kind and status — no Step fields — plus boards, card types and the sprint in outline. On an Aim board grouped by milestone, each milestone lists its Aims (`aims`: id and title; Aims in no milestone are under `unplacedAims`) in place of the board's flat `columns`: an Aim's `id` is what addOutcome and setAimMilestone take as `aimColumnId`. Narrow it to read what you need in full: `refs` for named cards with all their fields, their subset values (`subsets`, e.g. { "Area": "MCP", "Priority": "High" }; `suggestedByAssistant` names those the assistant set that no person has kept yet), their outcome and their linked cards one hop away (blocks, blockedBy, relates, and cameFrom / produced between a card and its Discussion); `outcome` for one outcome with its open Steps listed (those at their type's end, Done or Killed, are counted and left out: `closed: true` lists them too; a closed Step named in `refs` is always returned); `sprint` for the running and planned sprints' cards. Without `set` it reads the board set open on screen; name a set to read another. Read before writing any op: cards are referenced by their ref.

set.description: A board set by its exact name. Omit for the open set. A name not found is answered with the exact name of every set, upkeep sets included; the index read lists them too (projects and otherSets).

refs.description: Cards to read in full, e.g. ["ABC-123"].

outcome.description: One outcome by ref: its fields and its open Steps listed; closed ones are counted, not listed.

closed.description: With `outcome`: true lists its closed Steps (at their type's end: Done, Verified, Killed) as well.

sprint.description: true: the running and planned sprints, their cards listed; in Focus cadence the item on Work (or, with Work empty, its suggestions for what to pull next, each with its reasons), the pull order and upkeep.

tools.name: card_moves
tools.description: For each card, its type, its status and every move out of that status under the card type's OWN process (the board's settings, not a fixed list): whether the move is ready, the field rules an op will REFUSE it on until met, the other rules the board's gate waits on, and advice. Call it before a setStatus so you meet the rules first instead of learning them from a refusal.

tools.name: apply_ops
tools.description: Apply a batch of board ops and get the result back in this reply: every op's outcome in order, with the error text of any that failed and the ref of every card it created or changed. Ops include addOutcome, addStep, setField, appendField, setStatus, setSubset, addCardDep, addToSprint and renameCard; a product working one Focus at a time refuses the sprint ops and is planned with addFocus, moveToFocus, rank and moveOn. When a reply says every card on Work is built, recommend what comes next: { "op": "setRecommendation", "ref": "ABC-7", "reason": "what building it showed" } (one card; an offer above the calculated suggestions, never pulled on its own). With Work empty, read_board { sprint: true } lists Work's suggestions, each with its reasons: answer "what's next" from them, and when the person picks one take it with { "op": "takeSuggestion", "reason": "milestone" } (a reason that suggestion lists), which puts it at the top of the pull order and onto Work. An op reaches a card by its ref: "ref" for the card itself, "outcomeRef" for an outcome ("outcome" takes an outcome's title; a ref given there is read as outcomeRef). { "op": "addStep", "outcomeRef": "ABC-3", "title": "…", "kind": "…", "status": "…", "fields": { "Why": "…" } } (kind, status and fields optional); { "op": "setField", "ref": "ABC-12", "field": "Evidence", "value": "…" } (appendField the same, adding to the field); { "op": "setStatus", "ref": "ABC-12", "status": "Built" }; { "op": "setOutcomeStatus", "outcomeRef": "ABC-3", "status": "Defined" }. An addOutcome names the board set it goes to, { "op": "addOutcome", "set": "<set name>", ... } (or "forProject"): in a workspace of several sets one that names none is refused with the whole batch. Deletions and re-plans (deleteStep, deleteOutcome, moveStep) belong in delete_or_replan; sent here they are HELD, the whole batch with them, until a person approves it in Oyah, and read_board shows what became of it under "held". Within one batch, a card created earlier is reached by its title, never its ref (refs are minted after the batch): setField and setStatus take it as "card", addCardDep as "card" and "blockedByCard" / "relatesToCard". A Discussion (the conversation behind cards, on the workspace’s Discussions board, read with set "Discussions") starts with { "op": "addDiscussion", "title": "the topic in a few words, e.g. Where a discussed card lands", "question": "what the person asked, in their words", "startedBy": "the person you are talking with" }. Signed in through the Oyah connector, Started by is filled with the signed-in person and startedBy is not needed. It also takes "summary", "decisions", "sources" and "openQuestions" (or "fields": { "Open questions": "…" } by label); a key it cannot take refuses it and nothing is started. A later op in the same batch names it by its title as "card". It is refused while an Open Discussion has the same title: carry on in that one. A card it produces names it at creation: "fromDiscussion": "<its ref, or its title in the same batch>" on addStep, addOutcome or planProject. An existing card is linked with addCardDep { "ref", "cameFromRef" }; a card has one origin. addStep without "kind" makes the type its outcome takes — a Step on a measured outcome, an Improvement on a standing one; read_board's outcome read says which, with its fields, as addStepMakes. An addStep whose "fields" names a field that type does not have is refused whole and nothing is made: correct the fields and send it once more. An addStep onto a standing outcome (upkeep) needs "notABet": one sentence on why the work moves no live outcome's measure; without it the op is refused with those measures listed, and the reason is kept on the card. An addStep onto a Proving or Achieved outcome is refused here (it reopens it): ask the person, then send it through delete_or_replan, or add it with "deferred": true. Read each addStep line's note: SHOWS ON NO BOARD means its outcome is not yet Defined, and SIMILAR CARDS EXIST names cards it may repeat. Acceptance is ticked by a QA run in a fresh context, never by the agent that built the card: when you have built one, call qa_brief { ref } and hand its brief to a fresh agent. Do not tell the person the card is ready, or hand it over, until the QA run reports. If you must say something meanwhile, say only that QA is running, and do not call the card ready. When it reports, tell them what it found: closed to Done, nothing is left for them to try (say it is done and waiting to merge); criteria left for a person, those are what they try; sent back to Building, say so: you fix it first. That run ticks each criterion it verified: { "op": "tickAcceptance", "ref": "ABC-12", "n": 2, "by": "assistant", "evidence": "the check that passed, or a one-line result" } (refused without evidence). The tester sees it as checked by you and only tries what is left. Never tick what only a person can judge (it looks right, it reads well, it goes where they expect). A card that is Built with every criterion ticked by you, and that changes no screen, closes to Done on its own, marked tested by you; the reply says so, or why it waits for a person. Done is tested, not merged: when its PR is on main, stamp its cards with { "op": "stampMerged", "refs": ["ABC-12"], "pr": "#75" }. Once a release has gone out and is confirmed live, cut it: { "op": "cutRelease", "name": "Release 42" } stamps Shipped in on every merged card in no release yet; read_board { sprint: true } then names the last release. A value you set for a person to confirm is a suggestion: { "op": "setSubset", "ref": "ABC-12", "subset": "Area", "option": "Board", "by": "assistant" }. The card shows it as suggested by you until a person keeps it or chooses another. A NEW PROJECT, planned, is one op: { "op": "planProject", "name": "Setlist", "idea": "the person's own words", "objective": "what the first version achieves, and for whom", "milestones": [{ "title": "what this milestone achieves", "by": "YYYY-MM-DD", "why": "…", "keyResults": [{ "name": "Bands sharing a setlist", "measuredIn": "bands", "now": "0", "target": "5" }], "aims": [{ "title": "what people will be able to do", "outcomes": [{ "title": "…", "measure": "…", "baseline": "0", "target": "…", "why": "…" }] }] }] }. Two or three milestones; the first with its Aims and two to four outcomes, later ones may have no Aims yet. It refuses a name already taken. Accept what the person accepts in chat with { "op": "acceptPlan", "forProject": "Setlist" } or acceptProposal (forProject plus one of objective: true, milestone, aim, outcome or ref); discard what they reject with discardProposal (same targeting), which takes what is still proposed under the piece with it and is refused over anything accepted.

tools.name: delete_or_replan
tools.description: Delete cards (deleteStep, deleteOutcome), re-plan a card onto another outcome (moveStep), or add a card to an outcome at Proving or Achieved (addStep: a reopen, which apply_ops refuses), and get the result back in this reply. Your tool asks the person before this call runs: that answer is the approval, and the ops apply at once. Only these four ops, in a batch of their own. Same op shapes as in apply_ops, e.g. { "op": "deleteStep", "ref": "ABC-12" } or { "op": "moveStep", "ref": "ABC-12", "toOutcomeRef": "ABC-3" }. A reopen's reply says where the outcome now waits.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Bring a card (by ref) or a board (by name, e.g. "Backlog") into view in every open copy of Oyah, without changing anything — use it when you start talking about a card or the queue. A copy with Follow on moves to it; one with Follow off shows a "Claude is on … · Show" note instead. apply_ops already brings the card it changed into view, so there is no need to show that one.

board.description: A board by the name on screen, e.g. "Backlog". The open set's board of that name is shown.

tools.name: qa_brief
tools.description: The QA playbook for one card: a brief for a FRESH agent (a subagent, or a new session) to check that the card does what its Acceptance says, trying each scenario the way its Build says. It ticks what passes, crosses what fails and sends a failed card back to Building. Call it when you have built a card, instead of ticking the card yourself, and hand the brief on: do not run it in the conversation that built the card. Do not tell the person the card is ready, or hand it over, until the QA run reports. If you must say something meanwhile, say only that QA is running, and do not call the card ready. When it reports, tell them what it found: closed to Done, nothing is left for them to try (say it is done and waiting to merge); criteria left for a person, those are what they try; sent back to Building, say so: you fix it first.

set.description: The board set the card is on, by name. Omit for the open set.

tools.name: tech_lead_brief
tools.description: The Tech Lead playbook for one Step (or Improvement, or diagnosed Bug): a brief for a FRESH agent (a subagent, or a new session) to check what the Step and its outcome say about the code against today's code, before the Step is designed. It appends a dated Code check to the Step's Evidence: each claim still true, stale or gone, the files a design starts from, and whether the Step is still needed. It changes no code and writes no Design. Call it before you design a Step. An Improvement's check goes to its Definition; a Bug's, before it is fixed, checks its Cause and goes there. Do not write the Step's Design, or design it in chat, until the Tech Lead's Code check is written on the Step. If you speak to the person meanwhile, say only that the check is running. Then design from what it wrote.

ref.description: The Step, Improvement or Bug to check, e.g. "ABC-12".

set.description: The board set the Step is on, by name. Omit for the open set.

instructions:
Oyah is the team's board; these tools reach the open Oyah app.
- Read before you write: read_board first, and address cards by their ref (the code on each card, e.g. ABC-123).
- Before moving a card's status, call card_moves for it. It lists what that card type's own process asks before each move:
  "op refuses" rules must be met first (write the field earlier in the same batch, before the setStatus);
  "board asks" and "advice" are the team's rules too — meet them, or say plainly that you moved without them.
- Each apply_ops reply is the record of what landed. Report from it, never from memory, and fix any FAIL before saying the work is recorded.
- A rename (renameCard) is an ordinary op: send it with apply_ops.
- Deletions and re-plans (deleteStep, deleteOutcome, moveStep) go through delete_or_replan, on their own. Your tool asks the
  person before that call runs, so their yes IS the approval and the ops apply at once. Use it only for what the person
  asked for, or say plainly that you are proposing it.
- Sent through apply_ops instead, those ops are HELD in Oyah for a person to approve, with the whole batch. read_board
  lists held batches under "held" with their state (waiting, approved, declined).
- Adding a card to an outcome at Proving (or Achieved) REOPENS it: the outcome goes back to be worked again and its
  measurement window starts again. Ask the person first, and send that addStep through delete_or_replan; apply_ops refuses it.

New work, and work the person confirms:
- Judge where new work goes by the MEASURES of the live outcomes, never by their titles. Work that moves a live
  outcome's number belongs to that outcome: say so and ask the person. Work that moves none is upkeep, on a standing
  outcome, and its addStep carries "notABet": one sentence on why it moves no live measure.
- Work that comes out of a conversation is a CANDIDATE until the person says to build it: addStep with no status. A
  discussion is not consent; build only what they have agreed to.
- When the person says a card at Testing works, close it to the end state card_moves names for it (a Step to Done, a
  Bug to Verified), and close only the card they confirmed. If it is unclear which, ask.
- A Done card with no PR stamp is tested but not on main. Merge it only where the person has said you may, otherwise
  say it is waiting to merge; once merged, stamp it: stampMerged { refs, pr }.
- Once a release is deployed and confirmed live, cut it: cutRelease { name }. It stamps Shipped in on every merged
  card in no release yet. Only for a release that has gone out.
- When you have built a card, do not tick its criteria yourself: you would be grading your own work. Call qa_brief
  { ref } and hand the brief it returns to a fresh agent (a subagent, or a new session) that reads only the card. Its
  ticks close the card; a criterion it crosses sends the card back to Building, for you to fix.
  Do not tell the person the card is ready, or hand it over, until the QA run reports. If you must say something meanwhile, say only that QA is running, and do not call the card ready. When it reports, tell them what it found: closed to Done, nothing is left for them to try (say it is done and waiting to merge); criteria left for a person, those are what they try; sent back to Building, say so: you fix it first.
- Before you design a Step, claim it (the move card_moves names for starting its design), then call tech_lead_brief
  { ref } and hand the brief to a fresh agent (a subagent, or a new
  session). It checks what the Step says about the code against today's code and writes what it found on the Step.
  Do not write the Step's Design, or design it in chat, until the Tech Lead's Code check is written on the Step. If you speak to the person meanwhile, say only that the check is running. Design from what it wrote, not from the Step as it was first planned. An Improvement is checked
  the same way; a diagnosed Bug before it is fixed, against its Cause.
- A Bug you trace to the card whose work caused it is linked to that card: addCardDep { ref, relatesToRef }. read_board
  { sprint: true } counts those links against the cards the assistant closed (assistantClosed).
- When you call a card a candidate for what comes next, put it on the board, not only in your reply: addToNextSprint
  where the product works in sprints, moveToFocus or rank where it works one Focus at a time.

Plan a new app first. Oyah exists to help the person plan before you build:
- When they ask you to build something new and no Oyah project covers it (read_board lists the workspace's "projects"),
  offer to plan it in Oyah first, in a line or two, before writing any code. If they say no, carry on as you would
  without Oyah and create nothing.
- Ask questions only when the idea is too thin to plan from, and then only two or three plain ones (who is it for, what
  would make a first version a win). If it does not say where it runs, ask whether it is for the web, phones or both:
  that changes the milestones. Otherwise propose straight away.
- Propose the WHOLE plan with one apply_ops op, planProject (its shape is in apply_ops). Every outcome carries a measure:
  a number that moves when the outcome works. Everything it makes is PROPOSED until the person accepts it.
- Then say in a few plain sentences what you proposed, and that it is on the project's Aim board in Oyah to accept, change
  or discard. Talk in their words, not Oyah's: they learn Objective, Milestone and Key Result by seeing them on the board.
- Build only once the plan is accepted (read_board shows "proposed" on what is not). If they accept or reject it in chat,
  send acceptPlan, acceptProposal or discardProposal; never accept or discard on their behalf otherwise.
- Once the plan is accepted, before building the first outcome, offer to talk about the look and the tech first (apps they
  like, the feel; where it runs, what they already use), and say you will pick sensible defaults if they skip. Either way,
  write the answers, or the defaults you chose, to the product with updateProduct { product, designBrief, stack: "custom",
  customStack, contextNotes }, so they are kept in Oyah and can be changed there. read_board shows them under "products";
  read them before you write any Step's Design.

Keep the discussion. A conversation ends with the session; a Discussion card on the workspace's Discussions board
keeps it, so the person can come back days later without re-explaining:
- When talking something through first produces a card or a decision, read the Discussions board first
  (read_board { set: "Discussions" }). If an Open one is on the same question, carry on in it instead of starting another.
- Otherwise start one with addDiscussion: a title naming the topic in a few words, its question in the
  person's own words, and a Summary you draft for them to correct. Every card it produces names it at creation with
  "fromDiscussion".
- At each checkpoint (a decision made, a card produced, a question answered), appendField a dated entry to Decisions and
  keep the Summary current. A decision that governs the code or the process is written where that is decided (the
  outcome's Approach, a decision record), and the Decisions entry points to it.
- When your reasoning rests on something you read (a web page, a document, a file), appendField it to Sources, one per
  source: its title, its address, and what it backed. The address is shown as a link.
- A card the discussion produces lands at the rung its first gate field opens once you have written that field (card_moves
  says which), and at its first rung otherwise. Do not hold that move for the person's approval: the Discussion says why.
- Before the session ends, settle it (setStatus Settled) or say what is still open. A question that belongs to a card is
  written on that card; Open questions holds only those with no card to go on, and Settled is refused while it holds any.
- When the person picks up something talked through before, read its Discussion first (read_board { set: "Discussions" },
  then its ref) and carry on from where it stands, without asking them to explain it again.
